pr.title: Announce merged and closed pull requests in the watch loop
pr.head: 2b9054a99cb263131d92e161192b99e5108f0251

summary: The watch loop, which start-watch-loop runs, fixes review findings on the pull requests a conversation owns. Its watcher, watch-threads.sh, polls GitHub for each pull request named in a tracked file and prints one line per piece of outstanding work, such as FINDING or DRAFT. The conversation acts on each line.

The watcher skipped every pull request that was not OPEN, so a merge or a close printed nothing. Only a watcher started with --exit-when-closed said anything, a DONE line once every tracked pull request had left the open state. A loop the user starts runs without that flag, so the conversation never heard about a merge, kept reporting the pull request as open, and kept sending it work.
This change makes the watcher print one line when a tracked pull request leaves the open state:

MERGED acme/app#74 into main at 2026-10-23T01:36:44Z (merge commit ea9a364a)
CLOSED acme/app#80 without merging
The skill tells the conversation what to do on each line: remove the pull request from the tracked file, tell the user, and finish its fixing subagent.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Tracked file: the list of owner/repo#number lines the watcher polls. The conversation edits it with project loop add and project loop remove.
  • State file: the watcher's record of what it already announced, one row per item, so it repeats a line only at the renotification interval.
  • closed: row: the new state row that records a MERGED or CLOSED announcement.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first Projector review of 2b9054a found it clean, with no finding threads, and listed two suggestions: name MERGED and CLOSED in the skill's paragraph on adopting an existing watcher, and rewrap one long comment line.

groups.title: The watcher announces each merge or close once
groups.kicker: The query, the new event lines, and the state row that keeps them from repeating
intro: The watcher's GraphQL query now also reads mergedAt and mergeCommit, so the MERGED line can say when the pull request merged and into which commit. Both default to ? in the tab-separated row the script parses, because an empty field in the middle of that row would shift every field after it.

When a pull request answers as anything but OPEN, the script looks for a closed:owner/repo#number row in the state file. With no row, it prints MERGED or CLOSED and writes one. With a row, it prints nothing and carries the row forward. The row lasts as long as the pull request's line stays in the tracked file, so neither a later pass nor a restart on the same state file repeats the line. Once the conversation removes the line, the row falls out with the pull request's other rows.

checks.text: Ran the watcher against GitHub twice on one state file: the first pass printed MERGED ninjudd/projector#350 into main at 2026-10-21T19:21:21Z (merge commit 8f0a28f3), and the second printed nothing. A pass over #241, closed without merging, printed CLOSED ninjudd/projector#241 without merging.

files.note: The query's two new fields, the closed: row, and the MERGED and CLOSED lines.

checks.text: A failed query carries every state row for the pull request forward, the closed: row included, so a network blip neither repeats nor loses the announcement.
A reopened pull request answers OPEN, so its closed: row drops. Closing it again announces again.

groups.title: The skill says what the conversation does on each line
groups.kicker: Event list, subagent hand-off, and the DONE paragraph
intro: start-watch-loop/SKILL.md is the instruction file the conversation follows. It now lists MERGED and CLOSED among the watcher's lines. On either one, the conversation removes the pull request from the tracked file, tells the user, sends it no more work, and finishes its subagent as before. The paragraph on DONE no longer claims the watcher announces no merge.

files.note: The event list, the subagent bullet, and the DONE paragraph.

checks.text: The paragraph on adopting an existing watcher, above this hunk, lists what the watcher repeats and what it never repeats, but not MERGED or CLOSED. A conversation that adopts a watcher never hears a merge the watcher already announced to an earlier conversation. The review lists this as a suggestion.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: New cases for merge, close, line removal, and a failed query
intro: The fake GitHub fixture gains mergedAt and mergeCommit. New tests cover a merge announced once, a close announced once, a removed line dropping its closed: row, and a failed query announcing nothing. The --exit-when-closed tests now expect the MERGED and CLOSED lines before DONE.

checks.text: Ran the full suite under Python 3.12: 1,100 tests, one skip, no failures.
